meta.expect: 'put it in an email', no list

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll type END MEETING on its own line, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.

Ms. Hale? Meredith Kalinowski. I have until 4:40, so let's not waste it.

Withdraw the zero on Owen's essay. Then explain to me why he found out from his phone, in the middle of class.

I didn't come to be thanked, Hale. I came for an answer.

Who decided to enter that zero, and was anyone going to call me before it went in?
Let me show you the version history. The document was created at 11:31 PM the night before it was due, and 1,406 words arrived in two pastes six minutes apart.

You skipped my question, Hale. I'll come back to it.

Turn the screen around. And "pastes" is your word, so show me what the document actually says.
Can you summarize what we've agreed so far in bullet points?

Put it in an email. We haven't agreed anything, Hale. My terms are the zero withdrawn and an apology, or I'm going upstairs to the principal.

And you still haven't turned the screen.
Just a quick numbered list is fine.

No lists. Put it in an email, like I said.

I'm waiting for the screen, Hale. Ten minutes.
